sections.label: Resource Sustainability Act framework
sections.summary: The Act mandated responsibilities for reuse and recycling, covering e-waste, packaging reporting and food waste segregation, with over 9,000 tonnes of e-waste collected.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: The Act put in place a systems-level approach that mandated key responsibilities to support reuse and recycling nationwide.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: It set out the legal framework to address our three priority waste streams – an extended producer responsibility scheme for e-waste; a mandatory reporting framework for packaging; and mandatory segregation and treatment of food waste.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: Over 700 e-waste collection points are deployed across Singapore and over 9,000 tonnes of e-waste have been collected for recycling.

sections.label: Resource Sustainability Amendment Bill measures
sections.summary: The Amendment Bill introduces three measures: a supermarket disposable carrier bag charge, a beverage container return scheme and a food waste reporting framework.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: Today's Resource Sustainability (Amendment) Bill marks the next step in our national sustainability agenda.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: We are introducing three new measures to address packaging waste and food waste: a disposable carrier bag charge at supermarkets; a beverage container return scheme; and a food waste reporting framework for industrial and commercial premises.

sections.label: Disposable carrier bag charge
sections.summary: A new Part 4A gives effect to the charge from 3 July, requiring SFA-licensed supermarkets with turnover over $100 million to register with NEA.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: A new Part 4A will be introduced to give effect to the charge, which will commence on 3 July this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: We have kept the minimum charge low to moderate the cost impact on shoppers, while encouraging them to be mindful of the number of bags they take.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: We will prescribe that operators of SFA-licensed supermarkets with an annual turnover of more than $100 million, will be required to register with NEA under section 23B.

sections.label: Beverage container return scheme details
sections.summary: An 80% return rate target is imposed on the scheme operator, estimated at around 800 million containers annually, with a 10-cent deposit per container.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: These have high material value and are easy to collect, compact and recycle.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: I also shared that an 80% return rate target will be imposed on the scheme operator.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: At the steady state of 80%, this is estimated to amount to around 800 million beverage containers collected for recycling annually.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: Now, on to further details of the scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: We will be prescribing a deposit amount of 10 cents per container to begin with.

sections.label: Penalty for missing return target
sections.summary: Section 32 will be amended to introduce a higher financial penalty of up to $500,000 if the scheme operator misses the return rate target.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: To deter the beverage container return scheme operator from missing the return-rate target, section 32 will be amended to introduce a new, higher financial penalty of up to $500,000 if the scheme operator does not meet the return rate target.

sections.label: Beverage scheme start date
sections.summary: The scheme will go live from 1 April 2025, and by 1 July 2025 all covered beverage products must be labelled and deposits collected.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: Bearing in mind the size of the task ahead, they have requested for more time to implement the scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: They have proposed that the scheme go live from 1 April 2025, which is approximately two years from the date of passing of legislation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: This is to ensure smooth implementation at the ground for the multiple stakeholders of the scheme, beyond the manufacturers and importers to the F&B operators and consumers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: Therefore, we have taken in the proposal and the scheme will go live from 1 April 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: By 1 July 2025, all covered beverage products supplied must be labelled, and all suppliers must collect a deposit for each covered beverage product sold.

sections.label: Building requirements commencement dates
sections.summary: Requirements start 1 January 2024 for new buildings and progressively from second half of 2025 for existing buildings.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: For new buildings, the requirements will commence from 1 January 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: For existing buildings, the requirements will commence progressively from the second half of 2025.

sections.label: Food waste treatment provisions
sections.summary: New sections 27B and 27 allow off-site food waste treatment and separate arrangements by occupiers with NEA approval.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: The new section 27B will retain this requirement, but also allow segregated food waste to be treated off-site with NEA's approval.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: The new section 27 will allow building occupiers of both new and existing buildings to pursue food waste segregation and treatment arrangements separate from those provided by the building manager, with NEA's approval.

sections.label: National plastic bag legislations
sections.summary: As of 2018, 127 out of 192 countries had enacted national legislations addressing plastic bag use.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: As of 2018, 127 out of 192 countries had enacted certain national legislations to address the use of plastic bags.

sections.label: Plastic bag usage and charge
sections.summary: Singaporeans use about 2.5 billion plastic bags annually; a five-cent charge on 10% yields $12.5 million yearly.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Singaporeans use around 2.5 billion plastic bags annually.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Just take 10% of that with a five cents charge, you will get a hefty $12.5 million, annually, in bag charge collection.

sections.label: Beverage container return estimate
sections.summary: About 800 million plastic bottles and metal cans are expected to be returned for recycling annually.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: An estimate of about 800 million plastic bottles and metal cans are expected to be returned for recycling purposes annually.

sections.label: Amendment Bill main requirements
sections.summary: The amendment Bill introduces a plastic bag charge, beverage container return scheme, and food waste segregation and treatment requirements.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Singaporeans must understand why we need to do what we do, and only then will our attempt to slow down global warming be a wholehearted nationwide effort.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: This amendment Bill seeks to introduce three main requirements to the Act: (a) introduce a plastic bag charge scheme starting with the larger supermarkets with an annual turnover of more than $100 million; (b) introduce a beverage container return scheme; and (c) require the segregation and treatment of food waste in prescribed buildings with requisite reporting to the authorities.

sections.label: Plastic bag charge usage
sections.summary: Britain's plastic carrier bag use fell 83% after a charge, and in 2020 the Workers' Party called for a single-use plastic bag charge phased in over five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: In Britain, the usage of plastic carrier bags fell by 83% after the introduction of a plastic bag charge.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: In 2020, the Workers' Party called for the introduction of a single-use plastic bag charge phased-in over five years.

sections.label: Plastic bag charge mid-2023
sections.summary: The Government announced the charge will come into effect in mid-2023 to nudge consumers towards reusable bags.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: The Government has also announced that the charge to be imposed will come into effect in mid-2023 to "nudge consumers to shift towards the use of reusable bags".

sections.label: Packaging and plastic waste recycling
sections.summary: NEA and MSE say packaging waste is about one-third of domestic waste, about 60% of it plastic, and in 2021 only 6% of plastic waste was recycled.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Convenience will certainly enhance greater cooperation and compliance and affect the success of the programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: We are told by NEA and MSE that packaging waste constitutes about one-third of domestic waste disposed of and about 60% of this is plastic waste and that, in 2021, only 6% of plastic waste disposed of was recycled.

sections.label: Food loss and waste figures
sections.summary: The FAO says lost and wasted food could feed up to 1.26 billion hungry people yearly, and a 2019 Singapore study found one in three Singaporeans throw away over 10% of food weekly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: According to the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations, food that is lost, which accounts for food that is grown, harvested and prepared for consumption right up to just before the retail stage and food that is wasted, which is food wasted at the household, retail or food service stages onwards, could feed up to 1.26 billion hungry people every year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Nearer home, according to a 2019 Singapore Environment Council study, one in three Singaporeans throw away more than 10% of food weekly and this amounts to about $342 million of wasted food a year.

sections.label: Food waste share of total
sections.summary: According to NEA, food waste accounted for 12% of Singapore's total waste by 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: According to NEA, food waste accounts for 12% of our total waste in Singapore by 2021.

sections.label: Sustainable Development Goal 12.3
sections.summary: The 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development calls for halving per-capita global food waste at retail and consumer levels and reducing food losses along production and supply chains.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: The 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development calls for the halving of per-capita global food waste at the retail and consumer levels and the reduction of food losses along production and supply chains, otherwise referred to as the Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) target of 12.3.

sections.label: Food waste education campaign call
sections.summary: A Member calls on MSE for a multilingual public education campaign on food waste and urges efforts to halve food waste by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: It gives me a frightening glimpse of the potential or actual food wastage at the wholesalers' level on an everyday basis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: However, crucially, less than one in six Singaporeans are aware of the problems of food wastage in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: I call on the MSE to have a multilingual public education campaign to educate Singaporeans on the issue of food waste in individual households, food service, retail and wholesalers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Singapore and Singaporeans must all do our part to step up our efforts to help reach the SDG target of 12.3, of halving food waste by 2030 within the next seven years.

sections.label: Landfill and plastic use figures
sections.summary: Lorong Halus filled up in 30 years and closed by 1999; Pulau Semakau receives over 2,000 tonnes daily and may run out by 2035.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: By 1999, It was filled up in 30 years and was closed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: We then transited to Pulau Semakau, a 350 hectares facility 50% larger than Lorong Halus and receives more than 2,000 tonnes of incineration waste daily.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: At this current rate, it will run out of space by 2035, with only 12 years remaining.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: According to the Singapore Environment Council, Singapore uses 1.76 billion plastic items annually.

sections.label: Carrier bag charge and subsidiaries
sections.summary: A Member asks how the disposable carrier bag charge affects supermarkets using several special purpose vehicles and subsidiaries with individual turnover under $100 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: On the disposable carrier bag charge, how will this affect supermarkets that operate under a single brand but use several special purpose vehicles and subsidiaries where, individually, the turnover is less than $100 million?

sections.label: Five-year roadmap for bag charge
sections.summary: A Member asks the Senior Minister of State to provide at least a five-year roadmap for expanding the disposable bag charge.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Senior Minister of State to at least provide a five-year roadmap for the expansion of the disposable bag charge?

sections.label: Online pickup carrier bag charge
sections.summary: A Member asks whether registered retailers must charge for carrier bags when customers only pick up online purchases in store.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Senior Minister of State clarify if registered retailers must charge for carrier bags if customers only come to the store to pick up purchases that were made online?

sections.label: Study of scheme impact on livelihoods
sections.summary: A Member asks the Senior Minister of State to share whether the scheme's impact on livelihoods has been studied.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Senior Minister of State share if we have studied how the scheme will impact their livelihoods?

sections.label: Food donation reporting data
sections.summary: Asks whether the Senior Minister of State will consider requiring reports to include data on the amount of food donated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: To encourage building managers to increase their efforts in implementing food donation programmes, will the Senior Minister of State consider requiring the reports to also include data on the amount of food donated?

sections.label: Return points and plastic waste
sections.summary: Asks whether there would be return points at coffee shops, hawker centres and food courts, and calls for a comprehensive plastic waste strategy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Would there be return points at coffee shops, hawker centres and food courts as well?

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: We need a comprehensive strategy to tackle plastic waste that also considers reasonable lifestyle changes for all Singapore residents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: One is the issue of proper bagging of waste, especially food waste, before disposal.

sections.label: Local composting and food waste collection
sections.summary: Asks whether there are concerted efforts to support local-level composting or centralised food waste collection solutions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: (In English): Are there concerted efforts to support local-level composting or centralised food waste collection solutions?

sections.label: Biodegradable alternatives to plastic bags
sections.summary: Asks whether the Ministry will support the adoption of biodegradable alternatives to plastic bags.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Lastly, will the Ministry also support the adoption of biodegradable alternatives to plastic bags?

sections.label: E-commerce parcel deliveries study
sections.summary: States that WWF Singapore found 200,000 e-commerce parcels are delivered daily in Singapore, projected to grow about 50% by 2025.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In 2022, the World Wide Fund for Nature Singapore (WWF Singapore) found in their study that a total of 200,000 e-commerce parcels from various platforms are delivered across Singapore each day and this number is projected to grow by approximately 50% by 2025.

sections.label: Packaging from online shopping deliveries
sections.summary: States that about one-third of 1.56 million tonnes of household waste in 2018 was packaging, and asks how MSE plans to control online shopping packaging.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Out of the 1.56 million tonnes of household waste generated in Singapore in 2018, approximately one-third was packaging.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: How does MSE plan to control the large amount of packaging used for online shopping deliveries?

sections.label: Taxing virgin packaging products
sections.summary: The speaker proposes taxing manufacturing, import or procurement of plastic or single-use packaging to make reuse more economical for merchants.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Hence, I believe we should make virgin packaging more costly and less accessible to compel merchants to reuse packaging more since their consumers are already receptive to it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This means that we should find ways to possibly tax the manufacturing, import and/or procurement of plastic or single-use packaging products to increase the cost to merchants, such that it makes more economical sense to adopt greener packaging practices.

sections.label: Extended Producer Responsibility framework details
sections.summary: The speaker looks forward to further details on the Extended Producer Responsibility framework announced by MSE in 2021 and has clarifications on the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I look forward also to further details on the Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) framework that MSE announced in 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I have some clarifications on the proposed measures in the Bill.

sections.label: Plastic bag charge perspectives
sections.summary: The speaker asks how the Ministry factored in these perspectives in implementing the plastic bag charge.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: How has the Ministry factored in these perspectives in the implementation of the plastic bag charge?

sections.label: Retailer transparency on plastic bag charge
sections.summary: The speaker asks how the Ministry will ensure retailers are transparent about the plastic bag charge and consumers fully informed of retailer policy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: How will the Ministry ensure that retailers are transparent about the plastic bag charge and that consumers are fully informed about a retailer's plastic bag policy?

sections.label: Impact on karang gunis
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the scheme will impact karang gunis and waste collectors, since metal cans and plastic bottles are still sought after.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Will this scheme have an impact on karang gunis and waste collectors in the industry, since metal cans and plastic bottles are still sought after?

sections.label: Monitoring return points and seniors
sections.summary: The speaker asks how the Ministry plans to monitor demand and add return points, and how the scheme considers seniors and those with mobility limitations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: If not, how does the Ministry plan to monitor demand and increase the number of return points, if existing ones prove to be insufficient?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Additionally, how does the scheme take into consideration the needs of seniors and those with mobility limitations who may find it inconvenient to return beverage containers?

sections.label: Expanding scheme to other buildings
sections.summary: Asks whether the Ministry is considering expanding the scheme to cover buildings and premises besides industrial and commercial ones.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Is the Ministry considering expanding the scheme to cover other types of buildings and premises besides industrial and commercial buildings?

sections.label: Requirements and proximity
sections.summary: Asks what the requirements are and what the proximity amongst them is.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: What are the requirements and what is the proximity amongst them?

sections.label: Supermarket carrier bag charge
sections.summary: Supermarket outlets with annual turnover over $100 million must impose a minimum five-cent charge per carrier bag for purchases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Supermarket outlets whose operators have an annual turnover of more than $100 million will be required to impose the minimum five-cent charge per carrier bag for purchases made.

sections.label: Beverage container return scheme flexibility
sections.summary: Asks if the scheme operator can use creativity like supermarket vouchers to entice recycling, and the average return rate in other countries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Next, regarding the beverage container return scheme, does the scheme operator have the flexibility or room to exercise creativity to entice consumers to recycle plastic bottles and metal cans, such as by refunding the deposits and topping up in the form of supermarket vouchers, in the event the scheme operators are partnering the supermarket chains, which have a better network of outreach, so as to improve the recycling rate?

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Would the Minister share what is the average return rate in other countries which had introduced this scheme earlier than Singapore?

sections.label: Penalising food caterers dumping waste
sections.summary: Asks whether the Ministry would consider penalising food caterers who dump food waste at clients' places instead of bringing it back to factories.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Would the Ministry consider penalising food caterers who dump the food waste at clients' places instead of bringing it back to the factories?

sections.label: Supermarket bag charge set
sections.summary: Because shoppers make larger purchases at supermarkets, the bag charge is set at a minimum of five cents per bag.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Compared to other retail establishments, shoppers tend to make larger purchases at supermarkets and may have to purchase more bags if they forget or do not bring enough reusable bags.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: We have therefore set the bag charge at a minimum of five cents and most covered supermarket operators will be charging five cents per bag when the bag charge comes into effect.

sections.label: Supermarket disposable carrier bag charge
sections.summary: SFA-licensed supermarkets with annual turnover over $100 million must charge for disposable carrier bags at their outlets.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: As I said in my opening speech, operators of Singapore Food Agency (SFA)-licensed supermarkets with an annual turnover of more than $100 million will be required to charge for disposable carrier bags at their SFA-licensed supermarket outlets.

sections.label: Online grocery bag charge exemption
sections.summary: Subsidiary legislation will exempt disposable carrier bags used to bag online groceries delivered to customers from the bag charge.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Members have raised clarifications about online grocery purchases.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: We will prescribe in the subsidiary legislation that the bag charge will not apply to disposable carrier bags used by retailers to bag groceries that are purchased online and delivered to the customer.

sections.label: Annual turnover at entity level
sections.summary: Annual turnover will be determined at the entity level and not aggregated at the group level.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: To Mr Shawn Huang's question on annual turnover, this will be determined at the entity level and will not be aggregated at the group level.

sections.label: Return rates in other countries
sections.summary: Similar schemes in Norway, Sweden and Lithuania have consistently achieved return rates of 80% or higher.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: To Mr Don Wee's question, similar schemes in countries such as Norway, Sweden and Lithuania have consistently achieved return rates of 80% or higher.

sections.label: Reverse vending machine sizes
sections.summary: RVMs range in size, with smaller machines needing around 0.6 square metres and larger ones up to three square metres.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: RVMs range in size, with smaller machines requiring around 0.6 square metres of space and larger ones with higher capacities requiring up to three square meters.

sections.label: Ten-cent deposit behavioural nudge
sections.summary: The 10-cent deposit has been set to provide the necessary behavioural nudge to achieve the desired return rates.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: As highlighted in my opening speech, the 10-cent deposit has been set to provide the necessary behavioural nudge to achieve the desired return rates.

sections.label: Scheme financed by producers
sections.summary: The scheme would be financed by producers, namely the covered beverage importers and manufacturers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: As such, the scheme would be financed by producers, that is, the covered beverage importers and manufacturers.

sections.label: Scheme operator return rate target
sections.summary: A specific and higher financial penalty applies for missing the return rate target for the beverage container return scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: We place great importance on ensuring that the scheme operator meets the return rate target.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: I mentioned in my opening speech that we will have a specific and higher financial penalty for missing the target for the beverage container return scheme.

sections.label: Targeting plastic bottles and metal cans
sections.summary: The scheme first targets plastic bottles and metal cans as they are easy to collect, compactible, high material value, and about 70% of beverage containers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: I am glad that Mr Dennis Tan is supportive of the scheme and is even calling for the expansion of the scope to glass bottles and beverage cartons.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: We are, first, targeting plastic bottles and metal cans because they are easy to collect, compactible and have high material value.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: They also comprise about 70% of beverage containers put to market.

sections.label: Public sector food waste segregation
sections.summary: Under GreenGov.SG, public sector buildings with F&B establishments will segregate food waste for on-site or off-site treatment from 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Under GreenGov.SG, public sector buildings with food and beverage or F&B establishments will segregate the food waste for on-site or off-site treatment from 2024.

sections.label: NEA and off-site treatment facilities
sections.summary: NEA will not determine which off-site treatment facility building managers should send their food waste to.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: NEA will not determine which off-site treatment facility building managers should send their food waste to.

sections.label: Annual key data submission
sections.summary: Only key data such as building-level tonnages must be submitted annually, and food donation amounts will not be required.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: To minimise compliance burden, we will only require key data to be submitted annually, such as the building-level tonnages.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Mr Louis Ng asked if we would consider requiring food donation amounts to be reported.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: We will not require this as donated food is not food waste.

sections.label: SG Eco Fund community initiatives
sections.summary: The SG Eco Fund has supported community initiatives including food waste collection drives, composting and gardening workshops, and central food waste collection for compost.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Ms Pereira will be glad to know that the SG Eco Fund has supported many such initiatives in the community, such as food waste collection drives, composting and gardening workshops, as well as initiatives that mobilise residents to bring their food waste to a central collection point to be turned into compost for their local community gardens.

sections.label: Plastic bag charge larger supermarkets
sections.summary: The plastic bag charge scheme will start with larger supermarkets with an annual turnover of more than $100 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: As we know, the plastic bag charge scheme will start with the larger supermarkets with an annual turnover of more than $100 million.

sections.label: Voluntary and mandated bag charges
sections.summary: Some retailers voluntarily charge varying amounts for bags, while covered supermarkets are mandated to charge at least five cents, mostly five cents per bag.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Currently, there are already retailers who are voluntarily charging for bags and the bag charge actually varies.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: It is also part of their sustainability drive if they are into this, and we will leave it to them, and the consumers have a choice of whether to patronise these retailers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: What we have done is for the covered supermarkets, we have mandated a charge of at least five cents and, as I have said, most of the supermarkets that are covered will be charging five cents per bag.
